title: Ananda and Rahula (Kern ch. 9)
hookLine: the attendant and the son receive their promises too

lines: THE NAMES AT THE END OF THE CREDITS.
cards: Stay for the end of a film's credits. Far down, in small type, is the person who held the umbrella between takes, the one who drove the actors at five in the morning. Somebody decided they belonged on the screen too.
Chapter nine of the Lotus Sutra is that part of the credits. Promises of future awakening have gone out to the great disciples, chapter after chapter.
Two people close to the Buddha have stood nearby the whole time: the man who walked beside him every day, and the boy who was his son. You met them both in year one.

teach.b: First, they ask. Ananda and Rahula think, what about us? They bow at the Buddha's feet and say it plainly: we have a claim here too.
One of us attends you and keeps your teaching; the other is your son. Name us, and our wish is fulfilled. Behind them a whole crowd of monks, some still in training and some finished, stand up too.
Second, Ananda. The Buddha answers with a story. Long ago, under a Buddha of a past age, he and Ananda set their minds on awakening together.
Ananda gave himself to hearing much; the Buddha gave himself to effort. So one woke first, and the other became the keeper of everything he heard. Neither road is left out.
Ananda will be a Buddha too, and hearing this, he remembers his own old vow. Third, Rahula. He will be the eldest son of future Buddhas, as he is the Buddha's son now.

Then a tender line, in paraphrase: Rahula's quiet practice, nobody knows it but me. The one always introduced as somebody's son has a practice of his own, and his father has been watching. Fourth, why it matters.

teach.h: NOBODY IS TOO CLOSE TO COUNT.
teach.b: Being close to someone great can feel like living in their shadow: the assistant, the sibling, the spouse, the well-known one's kid, thanked in passing if at all.
Chapter nine stops and gives each a future with their own name and story.
Then it turns to the crowd behind them and gives them promises too.

how: Buddhist communities remember Ananda as the attendant who heard and kept the Buddha's teaching, and Rahula as his son who became a monk; in the Lotus Sutra both receive the promise of future buddhahood in chapter nine.

the Buddha promises him buddhahood too, and tells the story of how they set out together.

games.q: you're Ananda. promises have gone out to the great disciples, one after another. you've walked beside the Buddha every day. what do you do?
o: wait quietly; maybe he'll get to you.
stand up with Rahula, bow, and ask.
step back: promises are for the great disciples.
games.why: Ananda and Rahula stand up, bow at his feet and ask, saying they have a claim too. the Buddha answers each of them by name.

practice: Bring to mind someone whose work makes another person's work possible: the nurse beside the surgeon, the parent who drove a gifted kid to every practice, the person who keeps the books at a place you love.
See their face and their hands, and silently say their name and one thing they do that nobody thanks them for. Then let them go and rest with the breath.

wordCard.voice: Ananda and Rahula. The attendant who kept the teaching, and the son with a quiet practice, both given their own promise. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit and Pali: joy, delight. the name of the Buddha's attendant.

carryVoice: Your line: them too. Standing close to greatness never made them only a shadow. That's today, done.
